messages:
Priya (acme-customer): hi, we started getting intermittent 504s from the hosted /v1/generate endpoint for our longest prompts. Happens ~5-10% of requests in the last 30m. No auth errors, just plain 504. Here is a sample curl and the raw response we saw.

Priya (acme-customer): ```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDCUST\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-30b","input":"<~2k token prompt>"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> ...
< HTTP/2 504
< content-type: application/json

{"error":"upstream request timeout","details":"envoy upstream request timeout"}
```

Alex (support): thanks — escalating to eng-sre and oncall. do you see the 504s only for long responses or also short ones?

Priya (acme-customer): mainly long-running completions (30s+). short requests <5s are fine. We've tried retrying a few times and sometimes it works. No change in client side timeouts.

Miguel (eng-sre): on it. can you share the exact endpoint, region, and approx RPS during the failures? also any request id headers from the response?

Priya (acme-customer): endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate region: us-west-2 roughly 12 RPS from our app. i captured an example response headers: 

```
:status: 504
x-request-id: 6a1f2c8b
content-type: application/json
```

Diane (oncall): grabbing edge logs now. @Miguel can you check envoy/ingress timeouts for that route? last deploys?

Miguel (eng-sre): pulling envoy stats from nodes serving us-west-2. seeing a spike in `upstream_rq_timeout` counters starting 2026-03-10T15:20Z. sample envoy log line: 

```
[2026-03-10T15:23:12.482Z] warning envoy proxy: upstream request timeout: request_id=6a1f2c8b route=/v1/generate upstream_host=10.5.2.33:8080 upstream_response_time=30.004s
```

Miguel (eng-sre): upstream response time ~30s then envoy returns 504. interestingly, the model pods show GPU compute spikes and then a steady output — sometimes the pod responds slightly after 30s and the response reaches client but usually it's cut by envoy.

Kai (platform): any recent change to ingress/Envoy timeouts? I remember a PR to tighten timeouts for idle connections last week.

Miguel (eng-sre): yes — PR #2345 adjusted `max_stream_duration` and `idle_timeout` for the HTTP2 listeners from 90s -> 25s to limit slow connections. That was rolled to canary early morning and then to prod in us-west-2 ~2026-03-10T14:50Z.

Diane (oncall): bingo. that timing lines up with the spike. but why does it only affect long model responses and not short ones? because long responses take >25s to produce first/last byte and envoy kills the stream.

Alex (support): @Priya sorry about impact. engineering working on quick rollback. in parallel can you do one temporary test for us: call the same request but with streaming enabled and see if you get early partial tokens? if you can reproduce with a single curl and capture timings that helps.

Priya (acme-customer): ok testing now, will report back in ~2 minutes.

Priya (acme-customer): streaming gave partial tokens but still 504 after ~25s. so streaming mitigates a bit but not enough for our long generation.

Miguel (eng-sre): planned mitigation — revert PR #2345 in canary and prod for listeners in us-west-2. also raise `max_stream_duration` back to 120s for long-running model routes. rolling now.

deploy-bot: Revert PR #2345 initiated by Miguel. Canaries: 2/3 healthy, promoting to us-west-2.

Miguel (eng-sre): after revert we're seeing `upstream_rq_timeout` counters drop immediately. sample logs post-rollback: 

```
[2026-03-10T15:34:21.101Z] info envoy proxy: upstream response completed: request_id=9c3d4f7a upstream_response_time=65.238s status=200
```

Priya (acme-customer): confirming — our app now receives full responses for the test requests. thanks for the quick turnaround.

Diane (oncall): root cause: aggressive reduction of HTTP2/stream timeouts in recent ingress config change which caused Envoy to cut long-running model responses (504). Not a model or compute failure.

Kai (platform): actions: 
- revert config rollback already done (incident mitigation)
- add config canary check that runs long-running model generation smoke tests against listeners before promoting timeouts 
- instrument alerting for `upstream_rq_timeout` rate > 1% over 5m for /v1/* routes 
- update runbook with guidance: if 504s spike for long responses, check `max_stream_duration`/`idle_timeout` changes first

Alex (support): i'll follow up with Priya with a postmortem and timeline + credit for impacted requests. Priya, we'll also share the runbook once updated. sorry again. :bow: 

Priya (acme-customer): appreciated. please cc my technical lead: techlead@acme.ai for the follow-up.

Miguel (eng-sre): follow-ups for engineering: PR to enforce canary smoke tests (ticket INF-672), add specific prometheus alert expr, and add a one-click rollback playbook.

Diane (oncall): closing incident thread — mitigation confirmed and monitoring in the next 2h. will reopen if regression.

Alex (support): postmortem pending, will tag incident id INC-2026-0310-504 and share in #incidents and #support-notifications.
